cafe.title: The Baseline Café
cafe.k: Coffee, aguas frescas and lunch on the terrace

arrival.p: The club on the old knoll between The Commons and the Design District: two tennis courts, four pickleball courts and a padel cage under tensile sails, a clubhouse with a café, a pro shop and lockers, and a terrace to watch from. Park your cart in the court by Gallery Lane.

tennis.k: Acrylic hard courts · north to south
tennis.p: Two hard courts laid north to south, so the low sun is never in a player's eyes: east in the morning, west and low by evening. Court 1 is the show court beside the stand; the club's coach runs her drills on court 2.

pickleball.p: Four pickleball courts in a row, with low dividers, a kitchen line on each side of the net and the ball machine on court 6. The sails are raked low to the west to hold off the afternoon sun.

padel.k: Glass and steel · ten by twenty metres
padel.p: Padel is played inside the walls: the glass ends and the side panels are part of the court, so the ball comes back off them. Doors at the net line on both sides.

stand.k: Three tiers on the show court
stand.p: Timber seats on three stone tiers, close enough to hear the ball. Sit down for a rally on court 1; the sail above keeps the stand in shade most of the afternoon.

lawn.k: Rig, boxes, kettlebells and a yoga corner
lawn.p: A turf lawn for warm-ups and training: a pull-up rig with rings, plyo boxes, a kettlebell rack, a short sprint lane and yoga mats under the terracotta sail.

lockers.p: Two walls of lockers, benches down the middle, a stone vanity with mirrors and fresh towels by the door.

wall.p: The club's name in bronze on a rammed earth wall, laid in lifts like the clubhouse itself, behind a stand of saguaro.

carts.p: Ten bays with chargers off Gallery Lane. The club is a cart and walking place: there is no car park.

sails.p: Each sail is pulled into a saddle between four masts, low on its west edge against the afternoon sun and high on the east. The floodlights hang under them, so at night the fabric glows from below.

cafe.p: Coffee, aguas frescas and lunch at the counter or out on the terrace.

pro.p: Racquets and paddles to try, club wear, grips and balls, and the stringing machine behind the counter.

machine.p: Ten balls from the machine. Press Space, E or click as each ball reaches you: on time is a return, perfect timing scores double. Return seven of ten for the club stamp.

coach.name: Coach Sana Calderón
greet: Racket back, eyes on the ball.

talk.t: Welcome to Crosswind. I run the clinics on court 2: mornings for juniors, evenings under the lights for everyone else. Want a tip?
Split step as your opponent hits, then turn your shoulders before the ball bounces. Most club players are late because they start the swing too late, not because they swing too slow.
Residents, guests from the lodges, the flight crews on their days off. Pickleball is busiest at dawn, tennis at sunset. The padel cage fills up after dinner.
Court 6. Ten balls, and you only have to time the swing. Seven returns and the club stamps your passport.

barista.name: Luca
greet: Grab a table on the terrace.

talk.t: Morning players get the first espresso, the evening crowd gets the aguas frescas. Order at the counter and I'll bring it out to the terrace.
The prickly pear agua fresca, every time. And the green chile wrap if you've just played two sets.

pro.name: Tess Harlan
greet: Demo racquets are on the wall.

talk.t: Demo racquets and paddles are on the wall: take one out to a court and bring it back. Grips, balls and club wear are at the counter, and I string racquets while you wait.
o: How do I book a court?

talk.t: Walk on if it's free, or ask me and I'll hold one. The lights come on at dusk and the courts stay open late.

terrace: The sails look amazing at night.
lawn: Ten more minutes on the rig.
pro: I should try a lighter racquet.
club: Rammed earth, like the old ranch walls.

game.k: Space, E or click as the ball reaches you · Esc to stop
game.doneK: E to play again · Esc to leave
